subject: Token-bounded tail-latency SLA amendment request — StrataHealth
messages:
From: Anika Sharma <anika@stratahealth.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@stratahealth.ai; rajiv.menon@stratahealth.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: token-bounded tail-latency in Dedicated SLA

Hi Soojin / Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. StrataHealth is moving toward a pilot that will serve low-latency clinical summarization queries during business hours and larger batch analysis overnight. For the real-time route we need stronger predictability than aggregate p95; specifically the customer is asking for a token-bounded tail-latency commitment (e.g., 99.9th-percentile token time under X ms for requests up to N tokens) for a set of reserved GPU nodes.

High-level asks from procurement:
- A deterministic tail-latency metric bounded by token-length (we can provide expected token distribution)
- A mechanism for reduced preemption during 8am–8pm local business window (soft-preemption ok if documented)
- Credits if the token-bounded metric is missed more than M times/month

We know these are non-standard asks; can you confirm feasibility, rough pricing delta for pinned capacity, and what observability hooks you would need from our side? Attaching a redline with our proposed language (PDF) and a small sample of the token distribution.

Thanks,
Anika
Head of Platform Partnerships
StrataHealth

Attachments: Strata_SLA_Redline_20251019.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Anika Sharma <anika@stratahealth.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai; david_kim@redwood.ai; lauren_bishop@redwood.ai; procure@stratahealth.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Oct 2025 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: token-bounded tail-latency in Dedicated SLA

Thanks Anika — appreciate the clear ask and the redline. Looping in Ben (sales) and David (SRE) to scope feasibility and expected operating impact; Lauren from legal will review proposed contract language.

Initial notes:
- We can offer a token-bounded tail-latency SLA for a dedicated pool, but it requires operational constraints: pinned hosts (no bursting to shared pools), explicit KV/prefix caching enabled, and a bounded max sequence length for the routed route.
- The maintenance/preemption window can be made "soft" during business hours with stricter notice and reduced probability of preemption; that will be a commercial add-on.
- We will need an agreed telemetry contract (push or read-only ingestion into our telemetry endpoint) so outages and tail events can be jointly computed.

Ben — can you outline the commercial delta? David — can you sketch the telemetry/observability expectations and an SLI/aggregation approach? Lauren — we'll share the redline and your high-level comments.

Regards,
Soojin
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Anika / team — quick commercial sketch so we have something concrete to discuss in the pilot SOW: 

Proposal (high level):
- Dedicated pinned node pool sized for expected concurrent real-time requests (we'll dimension after we get token distribution). Pricing: base reserved capacity + a deterministic-SLA premium (ballpark +20–30% on dedicated monthly commitment depending on size).
- Soft preemption carveout: add-on that reduces preemption probability during the 8am–8pm window; includes a 4-hour advance notice for planned maintenance that might cause disruption during that window.
- Credit structure: a graduated crediting model. For a single missed token-bounded event we propose a 5% credit of the monthly dedicated fee, up to a cap of 50% after repeated misses. We can refine numbers.

I agree we need the telemetry contract. From a sales perspective, the things that materially change price are pinned capacity and the SLA premium; observability requirements are engineering-level and shouldn't affect the list price much but will affect onboarding time.

Next step: David, can you produce a short SLI/metric proposal (what to measure, how we compute token-bounded tail) so we can attach it to the SOW? Lauren, any major legal blockers on the redline we should anticipate?

Best,
Ben
Director, Enterprise Accounts

Subject: Re: Request: token-bounded tail-latency in Dedicated SLA — SLI proposal

Hi all — attaching a short telemetry sample and SLI suggestion. Summary below, full example attached (tail-latency-telemetry-sample.csv).

Suggested SLI / measurement approach:
- Unit: token-transit-time (ms) measured per-inference token generation event (from request arrival to token emission time on our router traces).
- Aggregation: compute 99.9th percentile of token-transit-time for requests with sequence length <= 512 and request concurrency <= reserved pool size.
- Bounding: the SLA will specify a numeric threshold (T ms) for the 99.9th token-transit-time for the covered route.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows (announced >= 4 hours) and force-majeure events; brief transient infra ramp-ups during scale-up after capacity changes (documented).

Operational requirements:
- Pinned hosts with no spillover to shared runtime.
- Unified KV prefix caching enabled for that tenant and warmed during the business window.
- A telemetry forwarder from Strata or a read-only telemetry pull (we can accommodate either) so both sides compute SLIs from the same raw traces.

If we can't pin hosts due to procurement constraints, the alternative is a probabilistic SLA with a larger threshold (higher T) and a larger credit pool.

Attaching the CSV sample: it contains a token-level trace for 1 hour of synthetic traffic and a calculator that produces p99.9 values.

-David
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: tail-latency-telemetry-sample.csv

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Anika Sharma <anika@stratahealth.ai>; soojin_lee@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai; david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Oct 2025 10:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: token-bounded tail-latency SLA amendment request — redline comments

Thanks — I reviewed Strata's redline (Strata_SLA_Redline_20251019.pdf). Top-level legal items and suggested edits: 

1) Limitation & credits: we will not accept open-ended unlimited exposure. Proposed company crediting model from Ben is a good starting point; I propose a monthly cap equal to the dedicated-monthly fee and a 12-month cumulative cap at 200% to limit indemnity exposure.
2) Measurement & dispute resolution: require a dual-source metric (Redwood and Strata compute the metric) and a 10-business-day dispute window with an independent arbitration step if unresolved.
3) Maintenance carveouts: define "soft preemption" precisely — e.g., Redwood will not preempt pinned hosts for capacity reasons during the business window except for <listed maintenance types>; any disruptive maintenance will include attempted mitigation and an attempt to run in a maintenance-reduced mode for up to 2 hours before full preemption.
4) Security/PII: ensure logs used for telemetry are redacted or tokenized; do not accept raw patient identifiers.

I can push a clean redline back to Strata if we agree to the credit cap and dispute mechanism. Otherwise, please flag other material changes.

Lauren Bishop
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
